clue:fresno.text: Julian’s song. He only plays it once a month. “You said the wall was where you yelled at God / I never heard Him yell back.” Lena left in the second chorus. So did I. Thursday the 8th, Margot was there. Lena by the window, alone. She left in the second chorus again.
clue:fresno.title: “Fresno”

clue:nora_box.text: A banker’s box in the RA storage closet since April: CALLOWAY · 222 · HOLD FOR FAMILY. HOLD underlined twice. A Selma High sweatshirt, CDs, a mug, a picture of two girls laughing in a dorm window — one of them Priya. A composition book. Inside the cover: Nora Calloway · Delgado 222 · If found, please return. Reward: I’ll sing you something. Priya has never gotten past that page. Nobody came for it. It lives in 401 now.
clue:nora_box.title: Hold for family

clue:plaque.text: Small brass plate under the candles: NORA GRACE CALLOWAY, 1989–2009. “Lord, to whom shall we go?” Somebody’s daughter.
clue:plaque.title: A plaque at the shrine

clue:postcard.text: She read the back of my postcard twice. Asked who A.H. was like she didn’t care. She cared.
clue:postcard.title: The postcard

note:alarm.text: Alarm 1, Monday the 31st, 3:07: everybody on the lawn in what they sleep in; Theo saved the espresso machine; Margot wrote ‘ALARM 1’ like it was a case number. Alarm 2, Friday the 18th, 3:12: eighteen days. Margot says that’s not a schedule, it’s a person. She’s keeping a log. Tuesday the 6th, nothing. Either the theory’s wrong or he’s on vacation. Alarm 3, Tuesday the 13th, 3:20, in a storm, under the overhang: twenty-five days. Margot says he’s irregular or he’s two people.
note:alarm.title: The 3 a.m. alarm

note:assignment.text: Two pages a week, bled on in red. Week two, hers: “That a Broken Statue Is Still Herakles,” with my sentence on page two. Mine: “That God Is the One Who Pays.” She kept it. Then Hale said it out loud: prove the thing you least believe you can prove. Moral luck — mine: “That the Lucky Man Owes Nothing.” Hers: “That There Is Such a Thing as Luck.” Her red on mine: “You don’t believe a word of this. It’s your best paper.” Friendship. Mine: “That a Man and a Woman Can Be Friends.” Hers: “That They Can’t.” She kept mine, and sent it back with *Defense.* in the margin. This week, lying. Mine: “That a Lie Can Be a Kindness.” Hers: “That Every Lie Is a Sin.” We agreed with each other for an hour. Hale asked for a priest.
note:assignment.title: Designated antagonists

note:bigsur.text: Six of us, one van, Highway 1. Father Osei blessed it at seven. South of Lucia a hose clamp backed off and it boiled over. A motel with one heater and a payphone. Kerouac cracked up under Bixby; we drove across it. Gorda gas. A turkey vulture, several times. A condor, once, with a number on its wing. Zebras. Six and oh.
note:bigsur.title: Big Sur

note:cigarette.text: An Altoids tin from a pea-soup restaurant in Buellton. RELIQUARY on the lid. No. 1: the Lighthouse. No. 2: Malibu, before breakfast. No. 3: the harbor — she smoked half of it first. No. 4: a clove, on the Delgado roof, at a wake. By dispensation. Do not ask. No. 5: the Ferrer Tower, in the bells. No. 6: Lucia, a motel porch, under the stars — on the back of the receipt. No. 7: Del Playa, on the widow’s walk, on the back of a HALO OR HORNS card. All Hallows — the occasion.
note:cigarette.title: The Reliquary

note:driveway.text: The guy at the end of the driveway is my TA.
note:driveway.title: The guy at the end of the driveway

note:fence.text: A gap in the fence behind the Lighthouse; a path along the bluff to the Point. Two people today told me not to go there. Neither would say why.
note:fence.title: The path

note:ferrer.text: A hundred and sixty steps. VIVOS VOCO · MORTUOS PLANGO · FULGURA FRANGO, around the biggest bell. I call the living, I mourn the dead, I break the lightning. One bell is flat. She says it isn’t. Thursday the fifteenth, at five in the morning, we played the Saints on it. Half of Anacapa turned its lights on. Nobody knows who. Margot’s following up for the *Tide*, from a minivan: the police log says one of them was laughing; the bass came in late twice. Nobody confessed.
note:ferrer.title: The Ferrer Tower

note:halloween.text: Theo’s party, on Del Playa. A staircase. Halo or horns. Four hundred Michael Jacksons. Laney was the Pope. Becca was the best saint in Las Olas. Everybody kept calling us American Gothic.
note:halloween.title: Saints & Sinners

note:la_flaca.text: Rafi’s bike, lent till Christmas. Not stolen. Abandoned. (A week’s difference, per his abuela.)
note:la_flaca.title: La Flaca

note:laney_advice.text: Laney Price, on romance: a poem, out loud, at a bonfire, about her eyes. It has to rhyme. And then — this is the important part — one knee. Not asking her again. I did the knee. Becca said: Not yet. Halloween: No.
note:laney_advice.title: Laney’s advice

note:ledger.text: Pie: paid. Bus fare: paid, with compliments. Richard Vance’s hundred: Theo’s, for the gas. A new *Brideshead*, cloth, with a ribbon: “Not on the tab.” Postage to Trumbull: $2.38, out of tips. Sully’s: a booth’s worth of nachos and my Cokes, on Meridian Pictures. Theo says Meridian can afford it.
note:ledger.title: The ledger

note:little_way.text: Thérèse of Lisieux. ICS, three dollars off the Driftwood cart, somebody’s highlighter quitting partway. My pencil: *Easy for you.* beside the elevator. *NO.* *She’d have hated Hale.* *Okay, fine.* beside the table of sinners. *Can a man and a woman be friends? Ask L.* beside her two brothers. I gave it to Lena at midnight on her feast. She wouldn’t let me erase a word. She kept it.
note:little_way.title: Story of a Soul

note:malibu.text: The bottom half of the pie Post-it, still on the espresso machine in Theo’s hand. Theo says it’s open. I believe him.
note:malibu.title: + 1 Malibu

note:newman.text: The roof is an upside-down boat. The lector reads Deuteronomy like he’s running for Congress. The cantor could make a rock cry.
note:newman.title: St. Brendan’s

note:nonna.text: Asked me about the girl. Laughed. Five minutes later she asked me again, the same words, like it was the first time. Ma says she’s tired. That was the nineteenth of September. Michaelmas she lit one for me and one for Danny. Saturday: ‘E la ragazza?’ Ma told her the girl has a boyfriend. ‘Peccato.’ Then, sharp: ‘E l’altra?’ Purdue Saturday. Dad said ‘Purdue’ and that was the call. Nonna got on the extension and called me Danny. Then she knew me. Then she asked about the crab girl.
note:nonna.title: Nonna

note:pelican.text: A girl across the quad won an argument with a parking cop while holding a lamp shaped like a pelican. I didn’t catch her name. I didn’t catch anything. Dad says close your mouth.
note:pelican.title: Pelican girl

note:pie.text: Marionberry: 4/10. Olallieberry: 9/10 — Dad would eat two pieces and complain about the second. Gloria rated Lena: pecan. She rated Margot without meeting her: rhubarb — tart, and nobody can decide if it’s a fruit. She rated Becca without meeting her: apple. Honest crust. Nobody loses sleep over an apple. Then she asked what happened to the pecan. A whole pie for a funeral is half price. I work here Tue/Thu/Sat, seven to one. Once a year the kitchen goes dark on a Thursday. Saturday the 10th Gloria met Becca: ‘Apple. Told you, hon.’ She looked at Wes a long time. ‘Peach.’ Everybody likes a peach, she says.
note:pie.title: The Anchor

note:pie_paid.text: Paid Theo one peach pie, Lena’s mother’s crust. Marionberry still 4/10.
note:pie_paid.title: Pie

note:record.text: Two–one after Labor Day; she paid her Sunday. Three–one after moral luck: mine; she said I argued it like it was mine. Now four–one. Friendship: mine, arguing both sides. She said she’d never forgive me. Wednesday she said she forgives me. I’d rather she hadn’t. Unofficial, the laundry room, midnight on her feast, no referee — the Little Way: Thérèse, on points. Unofficial, the Delgado kitchen, a Sunday, no referee — the rich young man: nobody won. She said: He looked at him and loved him. The roux came out perfect. Unofficial, the Brick, four in the morning, no referee — on the heart: nobody won. Official, Hale’s seminar, the day after the Anglicans — on leaving: mine. Five–one. Hale says I argued for leaving like a man who’s never been allowed to. Unofficial, Seacliff Road, Halloween, the hour that happened twice, no referee — on grace: hers. She wants to be asked.
note:record.title: Duels with Lena

note:roof.text: Fifth floor: EMERGENCY EXIT ONLY · ALARM WILL SOUND, and under it, in Sharpie gone brown: (it won’t). It doesn’t. A popsicle stick in the strike. Tar, gravel, the elevator housing, a parapet to the hip. The Lagoon one way, the hills the other.
note:roof.title: The roof

note:seminar.text: Hale’s seminar. Monday, 1 p.m., Hollis 302. One of the twelve is M. Broussard.
note:seminar.title: PHIL 9H

note:soprano.text: Parish hall, bulletins, lemon bars. “We lost our best soprano last spring.”
note:soprano.title: Mrs. Fitch

note:talk.text: Peter Haddad and Kenzie Rourke, Newman’s it couple, tell their chastity story with a slideshow: Steubenville, 2007; Disneyland; a cousin’s wedding. Margot read them Ephesians. Kenzie answered with verse 25, better than the text deserved. Peter makes the call. Prayerfully.
note:talk.title: Love Is Patient

note:the_point.text: A cliff, according to Priya. Nobody goes there after dark. Her rule, not the school’s. Now I know whose rule it is. Went up on Halloween, the second one o’clock, looking for Laney. The old light, dark since 1967. A low stone wall, knee-high on my side and nothing on the other. A white cross: NORA. Somebody’s flowers, two weeks dead, on kitchen string.
note:the_point.title: The Point

note:theo_dawn.text: Came in barefoot at 5:20, sand and wet jeans. ‘Couldn’t sleep.’ There was a girl in our room. Sunday, Sept. 20, 6:10, wet to the shins and hay on his sweater: he says he runs now. Four miles. Barefoot. Sunday, Oct. 11, before light: wet to the shins again. He drives to where he runs. Sunday, Oct. 25, before light, at a motel above Lucia: up the path from the water, wet to the shin, sand on the cashmere. ‘Couldn’t sleep. Went to look at the ocean.’ Sunday, Nov. 1, Halloween’s morning after: asleep on his covers in the dinner jacket at seven, shoes on, sand to the knees, the hems wet.
note:theo_dawn.title: Theo, before light

note:whiteboard.text: Margot’s, by annexation: USEFUL IDIOTS FOR CHRISTIAN NATIONALISM, COSTIGAN | BROUSSARD. Sully’s made the board: liturgical football, idolatry, my outfit. Margot wasn’t even there when I read it. She didn’t need to be. Now the chastity talk is up there too: both of us, voluntarily. Kenzie Rourke got her own line. Margot thinks she might not be an idiot. Category pending. C 6, B 5. The morning after the wake, under the total: TUESDAY — NO SCORE. (BEREAVEMENT.) October 9th, top of the board: LEIF ERIKSON DAY (OBSERVED). Columbus: see attached. Then: FERRER TOWER · THU 5:00 A.M. · “WHEN THE SAINTS GO MARCHING IN.” Suspects: a Catholic; a different Catholic. Laney added the Holy Ghost. Margot wrote it up for the Tide and didn’t name anybody.
note:whiteboard.title: The whiteboard

person:becca.text: Coeur d’Alene. Seven siblings; wants seven or nine kids, odd numbers, for the tiebreaker. Can butcher a deer — elk too. Has pulled a calf, and it shows. Ran the beach cleanup like a cattle drive and put me on her team. Asked about the scar in the water. Told her mother the cleanup was a date, then asked me if it was. Wrote FRIDAY? on her clipboard, and meant it. Drives her brother Eli’s red Ranger; St. Isidore on the visor. Second date: Friday-night football. Knows downs. Prayed a Glory Be on fourth and one. Learned the First Way on the bleachers and said it back perfectly. Kissed my cheek so there’s no confusion. Third date was mine. I asked. I paid. The elephant seals at Piedras Blancas at sunset, in Kevin’s Odyssey. She knew what every one of them weighed. Nobody’s ever planned a thing for her, she says. She’s been praying for two in the morning. Named a hermit crab Thomas, after the First Way, and asked Fr. Osei whose blessing it was. Works the Marine Lab touch tank Thursday afternoons and Friday at six in the morning — that’s how she signed Thomas out. He’s home; she knows him by the chip in his shell. Mailed Rosie a birthday card with Thomas on it and six true facts on the back, to the address I gave her for her Christmas cards. She does them in October. Has a page on her clipboard for Wes. She’s been praying for him and Lena since September. Her eyes are gray. Brought a survival bag to the library for my midterm, with a clementine for Lena. Prays at two, like always. Took me to *Where the Wild Things Are* at the Rialto; her favorite line is the last one. My mother wrote her a thank-you note. Her list for Halloween says WE SHOULD MATCH!! It’s due Halloween. She says I look at her like homework. She says she’ll wait. Stuck on the touch tank all weekend while we were at Big Sur: the weekend volunteer has the swine flu. Asked me for the monks’ fruitcake for her Grandma Agnes — the only honest fruitcake in America. I handed in my homework six days early. St. Isidore and St. Maria: her first. Early, she said. Nobody’s early but her. Halloween: she sewed my costume out of a Rathdrum Feed & Seed sack. She was St. Maria de la Cabeza in Mrs. Fitch’s lace, with a water jug. Best Saint, by acclamation — a gold halo. Never won anything that wasn’t a heifer. Home at 11:40 for the six o’clock tank; the volunteer still has the flu. ‘Farmer.’
person:becca.title: Becca Lindell

person:caleb.text: Visalia. Has Hale’s book so full of Post-its it’s molting. Says ‘Selah’ when he means ‘touché.’
person:caleb.title: Caleb (PHIL 9H)

person:dale.text: Dale Wisniewski. A Lions fan alone at the end of Sully’s bar in a Barry Sanders jersey. Warren, Michigan — not the other one. Tips in quarters. Said the rookie’s going to be good.
person:dale.title: Dale (Sully’s)

person:danny.text: My brother. Trumbull Correctional. Calls me Professor. Ma brought him the good socks. *Brideshead* went to him through Driftwood, margins erased; the C.O. reading it first says it’s about a house. The ocean letter got there; Reggie, from Portsmouth, decided on his own the Pacific smells like money and fish. Lena knows. She asked his name. On the bluff bench she said hi to him and told him she’s going to be defense, and he laughed like he used to. The system cut him off at ‘tell Gina — .’ He wrote the rest down: tell Gina it ain’t hers to carry. He’s got it. On Michaelmas he wrote: Tell Lena hey. I like knowing it. You sound happy out there. Don’t feel bad about it. That’s an order. Lena says hey back. She said it herself. The Saints are four and oh, and she expects him to know that. Third letter, after Columbus Day: the Hopkins got there. He read Ma “Felix Randal” on the phone and she cried; he says he’s telling me so I know he read it, not so I feel bad. The Housman made Reggie cry. Ma told him about Becca. He wants to know if I told Lena hey, or does he have to come out here. I did. He doesn’t know yet. Push-ups: 140.
person:danny.title: Danny Costigan

person:evan.text: Thursday section, Hollis 108. Kierkegaard. Kind to the scared ones, murder on the lazy ones. Smokes American Spirits. Rides a bike. Came back from PERSONAL grayer. Told us we’d left out a driver. Says Kierkegaard was engaged once, gave back the ring, and wrote about her for the rest of his life. Gave back the midterms, then read us Kierkegaard on recollecting the dead — the freest love, because they can’t pay you back. Couldn’t finish the paragraph.
person:evan.title: Evan Marsh (TA)

person:frank.text: Frank Costigan. Twenty-six years on the line at Lordstown, laid off since June. Drove me 2,400 miles because two plane tickets cost more than the truck is worth. Saw the Pacific for the first time today. Didn’t say anything. That’s how you know.
person:frank.title: Dad

person:gina.text: My sister. Fifteen, a sophomore at Ursuline. Texts in lowercase like punctuation costs extra. A girl in religion class called her the class expert on visiting the imprisoned. Dad turned the radio back on. Nonna told the altar society I went to confession. Said Danny’s name back to the girl. The girl looked away first. Then laughed with Kelsey anyway. Gina wants the first part on the record. She wanted to know if the nun was real. Now they’re Facebook friends, and Lena signs her wall posts like letters. Gina found the boyfriend in about four minutes. Didn’t tell Nonna. Ashley Vrabel is going to Halloween as a prisoner. Orange jumpsuit. A tribute, she says. Lena read it once and gave me a line for her. Halloween: went as a nun, obviously. Ashley wore the jumpsuit. Gina said it — visit, not dress up as — and Kelsey laughed at Ashley for once. Ashley says she’s dead Monday.
person:gina.title: Gina

person:gloria.text: Hired me for rating her pie a four. Rated me a lattice-top. I’m not going to ask.
person:gloria.title: Gloria (the Anchor)

person:hale.text: Wrote *The Consolations of Disbelief*. Wrote me a postcard. Walked into Hollis 302 at 1:07 with wine on his cuff and asked us to prove we have souls. Saw my face at the Anchor before he could put it to the nine pages. Called me a spaniel. Some nights he drinks alone in the Anchor’s back booth after midnight and says Housman to the window. Tips like he’s apologizing. Wrote his doctorate on moral luck. Asked me if the lucky one sleeps. Lent me his own copy of Williams’s *Moral Luck*, his Oxford pencil arguing with Williams in the margins on a first-name basis. Wants it back with mine in it. I owe him more than one. Gave me a pocket Housman for Danny, foxed, wartime. No margins. They’d only erase them. Has a deaf old greyhound named Bishop Berkeley. Brought him to the Blessing of the Animals to annoy Fr. Osei. Osei finished his limerick for him. Asked me if the Housman had gone. Says when you leave something, look at it. Newman did.
person:hale.title: Prof. Adrian Hale

person:julian.text: The guitar guy from the Lighthouse stairs. Plays Bastille Thursdays. Wrote a song called “Fresno.” Plays it once a month.
person:julian.title: Julian

person:kevin.text: Kevin Tran. Goes to daily Mass, saves you a seat with a Bible. Has a sister, Tina, in dental school, who flossed in the womb. Lies to his mom about orgo in Vietnamese. Drives his mother’s Odyssey at sixty-five, not sixty-six. His dad has two nail-salon supply stores in San Jose and has never had a Labor Day. Brought six pairs of gloves to a beach cleanup. Mouthed every word of Joey’s first reading from the second pew. Somebody coached Joey; I can guess who. Brought tea to a wake. His Bà Nội says heaven makes the elephant and heaven makes the grass. Walked Margot down at four in the morning. Handed Lena a roll of quarters for the payphone before she asked. Halloween: All Saints, every one nobody’s heard of — scrubs, a halo and a white mask. He found Laney.
person:kevin.title: Kevin Tran

person:laney.text: Laney Price. Pi Lam, as of Thursday: ran back across Seacliff in a pink cowboy hat to Lena first. The night before, on the floor of 217 in a white dress, she asked what happens if they look at her and see. First Catholic Mass: arms crossed like a Baptist, came back from the blessing pink and quiet. Programmed herself into my phone. (Hoodie status: hers.) Pi Lam’s barn party: carried upstairs by her new sisters, glorious and wrecked. Called Lena a mother over the banister. Said sorry at the sign of peace, at her second Mass. Big/Little: Sloane is her big. On the front steps at one in the morning, in a PI LAM LITTLE shirt, with a balloon on her wrist, she told me about Kaylee Whitmore. Fifteen; Kaylee drove; they’d both been drinking and Laney let her. Preston Road. A culvert. A cast for six weeks that everybody signed. A month later, a doctor’s note for flying; she’d never been on a plane. Lena’s the only other one who knows. In the water at Pfeiffer Beach she caught my swan. It’s Theo’s. Her fourth Mass, up a mountain with the monks. Asked Lena how you light a candle, and lit one. Don’t you dare, she said. Halloween: Pope Joan, in a cardboard mitre with gold rickrack. Blessed Del Playa from the widow’s walk until Rafi’s father asked her to come down. Over a bullhorn. Best Couple, with Margot. Went missing with three pledges for most of the extra hour; Kevin found her at Lupe’s with a burrito. She’s not stupid. She’s hungry.
person:laney.title: Laney Price

person:lena.text: New Orleans. Two seventeen. Classics. Hale paired us for the semester. Makes a roux like she’s taking a vow and expects you to keep up. Her father sells Gulf shrimp — Broussard’s Seafood, Banks Street. Boyfriend: Wes Arceneaux — Tulane, civil engineering, the boat at sixteen. Calls at 8:04 on the dot. Her grandmother, Lucille Guidry, died in the storm in ’05; they buried her in November, in the good dress. The medal came back to her mother in a plastic bag. She has never asked her mother one question. The year after, she went to Mass every morning to yell at God, and somewhere in there it stopped being a fight. Paints a mean fleur-de-lis. Said hi to Danny. Says she’s going to be defense. Walked her home the long way from Pi Lam: the beach, the creek, the tower, the Commons, the Lagoon bench. Wes calls from somewhere loud lately; her brother Luc is with him. She’s decided not to notice. The Tuesday of the wake he called on the dot, from his room. He came for Columbus Day weekend to see the Pacific. She’d told him it’s a threat. He touched it at two in the morning. Came to Marisol for the money, she says — Notre Dame gave her half. Went to Hale’s office to tell him he was wrong about who gets to forgive. Cried for Anders on the roof and didn’t give an inch. Stayed till the chimes. There’s a sentence she hasn’t finished. Her middle name is Thérèse; October first is her feast. She erased *Show Lena* out of the Hopkins herself, so Danny could have it. At midnight I gave her *Story of a Soul* with my margins in it, and she wouldn’t let me erase a word. On the beach she asked if I know what I’m doing. I don’t. She laughed. At the elevator: ‘That was a terrible thing to be glad about.’ Brought Wes to everything. Wouldn’t walk past the last house on Seacliff toward the Point; said she was cold. At the stove she gave Becca the spoon. Monday night, two floors down, on the phone to New Orleans: ‘He’s my friend, Wes.’ Plays the piano in the Delgado basement — the one nobody admits to playing. Two years at the Rosary. At five in the morning she played the Saints on the Ferrer carillon with her fists, one bell flat, and said it wasn’t flat, it was New Orleans. Wes told her what I said on the beach, and what I didn’t. On a motel porch above Lucia at three in the morning she told me I can’t say her name like that. She asked what I decided. Not to be the one who wrecks anything, I said. She said okay. Then: me neither. Bought her Mémère a fruitcake from the monks, in exact change. ‘A girl writes the thing she wants first, Youngstown.’ Halloween: Flannery O’Connor, with a stuffed peacock tagged 57. Andalusia. She wouldn’t go past the last house on Seacliff, not even for Laney. ‘I came as her. I never said she was right.’ In the last minute of the extra hour, she put my hat back on.
person:lena.title: Lena Broussard

person:margot.text: Margot Lindqvist. Has a folder on me. Called Lena and me useful idiots for Christian nationalism in front of four hundred people. Made a point about the Euthyphro I still can’t answer. Her mother teaches Classics at Reed. Held a wake for a cigarette on the roof and buried it at sea, for the prose. Had a brother. Her mother was forty-one; the test came back; they’d already picked the name. Anders. March 15, 2000. She’s defended her mother in every room since, and she defended her on the roof. Lena said his name. Doesn’t sleep. My friend. She has a faith column now, in the *Tide*, on a trial basis. If it’s boring they’ll kill it. She told me not to be boring. Came to Big Sur as an observer, for the monks — a functioning patriarchy in its natural habitat. Ran the *Tide*’s Ferrer follow-up from a minivan and wrote nothing down. Sunday at the coffee urn: ‘I’m not writing anything down.’ Halloween: Joan of Arc in duct tape, with her own haircut. Best Couple, with Pope Joan. She called it a category error and laughed anyway.
person:margot.title: Margot Lindqvist

person:nora.text: The name on the plaque. Priya’s freshman roommate, Delgado 222. From Selma — raisins. Sang soprano; sang the Memorare in the shower. Philosophy. Fell at the Point at the end of April. September 8th would have been her twentieth birthday. Facebook won’t stop suggesting her. Her things are in a box in Priya’s room now. On the inside cover of her journal she promised whoever found it a song.
person:nora.title: Nora Calloway

person:osei.text: Newman chaplain. Kumasi, Ghana. Used to be a doctor. Limps and doesn’t mention it. Plays chess like he’s got all night and highlife like the neighbors owe him money. Told me a proverb about funerals. I laughed. That was apparently the point. Said Nonna’s Mass himself at the 12:10, like he promised. Gave me a card for her: ‘A grandmother likes paper.’ Blessed Hale’s deaf dog with his hand on its ribs, where it could hear. Finished Hale’s limerick for him. Laughed for a full minute at Becca’s crab.
person:osei.title: Fr. Gabriel Osei

person:poppy.text: Theo’s sister. Fourteen. He always picks up.
person:poppy.title: Poppy

person:priya.text: Laminates things. Owns an air horn. Her freshman roommate was Nora Calloway. The one rule she doesn’t laminate is for her. Three jobs: RA, the library overnight desk, orgo tutor. Failing orgo, she says. Her parents run a motel in Fremont and think she’s going to be a doctor. Re-laminated the laundry room at two in the morning, on her twenty-first birthday. Her mother’s text came in at the dryers. She didn’t answer it in front of me.
person:priya.title: Priya (RA)

person:rafi.text: Rafi Ochoa. Second floor. Carried my fridge up four flights and was gone before Dad could tip him. Calls everybody boss. Lent me his bike on the wharf at one in the morning like it was nothing, till Christmas. His father’s a detective. He sells weed, and Adderall around midterms. Not bars, he says.
person:rafi.title: Rafi Ochoa (204)

person:ray.text: Detective Sergeant, per the badge wallet. Rafi’s father. Gray Crown Vic, a windbreaker, the Vehicle Code by heart. Knows my face from the Anchor counter: Tuesdays, meatloaf, a nod to Rudy. Did the bit: ‘License and registration.’ Asked what was in the bag and took ‘vitamins’ for an answer. Gave me a light out of his trunk. Found property.
person:ray.title: Ray Ochoa (Marisol PD)

person:richard.text: Theo’s father. Learned everybody’s name in one pass but mine; thought I came with the caterer. Calls him Teddy. Stayed six minutes, fourteen seconds. Margot timed it.
person:richard.title: Richard Vance

person:rudy.text: Line cook. Rosary on his wrist, a ballgame on the radio, Louis L’Amour in his apron. Did six years at Soledad. His mother came every other Sunday — three buses from Oxnard. Says: write him, even when there’s nothing to say.
person:rudy.title: Rudy (the Anchor)

person:theo.text: Roommate. Drives his grandfather’s car like a getaway. His father calls him Teddy and stays six minutes. Heard my brother’s voice and didn’t ask. Loves *Point Break* with no irony at all. Poppy texts him at midnight. The Big Sur Expedition, on his father’s letterhead. Called the Anchor and got my Saturday covered before I could say I work Saturdays. Bought six used copies of Kerouac off the cart at Driftwood. Halloween: threw the party of the year as Gatsby. Left it at twelve-thirty by the back gate. Found him at the wall at the Point at one in the morning, the second one. He said not there.
person:theo.title: Theo Vance

person:tony.text: Lena’s father. Broussard’s Seafood, Banks Street. Twenty-eight years in the same seats. Held the phone up to the kitchen radio for the whole second half while we lost him at every curve on Highway 1. Wes told him there’s a Browns fan out here. Laney had him at hello.
person:tony.title: Tony Broussard

person:wes.text: Lena’s boyfriend. Tulane, civil engineering; the boat at sixteen. Six-two, a chipped front tooth, a Saints cap he’s been bending since 2006. Calls me the Ohio guy. Says she called me a jagoff and that means she likes me; he’s known her since she had a retainer. Drank the Pacific: the jar came back empty. Theo fetched him from the airport alone, in a two-seater, with a sign, and cancelled his motel. Bedbugs, Theo says. He’s on Theo’s new air mattress in our room, three nights. The Corps built the walls wrong; he’s going to build them right. I like him. Saturday night on the beach at Campus Point he waded into the Pacific to the knees. At sixteen he pulled people off roofs for four days in his uncle’s boat. There was one he couldn’t get to — a woman in an attic on Pauger Street; the axe wouldn’t go through. He couldn’t kneel for a year after. Then she came along, he says, and he could. Her Mémère gave him a ring at Easter, for when. He’s going to ask her father after she graduates. He asked me not to say anything to her. He asked me to take care of her.
person:wes.title: Wes Arceneaux

person:yusuf.text: Fremont. Engineer. Fasting for Ramadan through a ninety-minute seminar and funnier than all of us. Broke the fast with his people on Mission Street and fed me till I couldn’t stand. Father on the NUMMI line since ’85. Brother Tariq interprets for the Army in Helmand and calls on Sundays.
person:yusuf.title: Yusuf (PHIL 9H)
